title: Elodie and the Cover
premise: Bram Whitlock, a veteran crash investigator, receives calls on a burner phone from his wife's voice — recordings that reveal Flight 4471 was brought down to silence a whistleblower carrying evidence of a transnational arms-laundering scheme. As Bram follows the recordings' clues across three countries, he discovers the cover-up is protected by an assassin named Voss and sanctioned by officials in all three governments, including the mentor who taught him everything. The inheritance at stake is both literal — his daughter's trust fund was seeded with laundered money — and moral: what he passes on to her if he survives. In the end Bram trades his own safety for the truth, broadcasting the flight data live before Voss can silence him, and survives wounded to rebuild a life with his daughter built on honesty instead of hush money.
about_author: Juniper Eriksen is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading accident reports most people never see. She writes thrillers about ordinary professionals who discover the machinery behind official truths.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Bram Whitlock wakes at 3:14 a.m., as always, in his empty house; POV Bram. At work he's assigned to audit closed files, where he notices Flight 4471's black-box timeline has a forty-second gap. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into professional suspicion.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: A package arrives containing a burner phone that rings — his dead wife Mara's voice plays a recording describing the cockpit in her final minutes. POV Bram. He verifies the number traces to nothing. Emotional beat: terror braided with desperate hope.

chapters.title: Forty Seconds
chapters.summary: Bram pulls the raw flight-data archive and confirms the gap matches Mara's recording exactly. His supervisor, Aldous Renner, gently warns him off. POV Bram, brief interlude of the assassin Voss watching Bram's office. Emotional beat: the first certainty that this was murder.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower
chapters.summary: The recordings name an engineer, Tomas Ilic, who died 'randomly' weeks after the crash. Bram flies to Belgrade against orders. POV Bram. Emotional beat: crossing the line from investigator to suspect.

chapters.title: Three Governments
chapters.summary: In Belgrade, a journalist, Petra Kovac, shows Bram matching anomalies in two other investigations across borders. Someone ransacks her flat hours later. POV alternating Bram/Petra. Emotional beat: alliance forged under threat.

chapters.title: Voss
chapters.summary: Voss eliminates a records clerk in Vienna and reports to an unnamed handler that Whitlock is 'waking up.' POV Voss — cold, procedural, oddly principled. Emotional beat: dread established through competence.

chapters.title: The Trust
chapters.summary: Bram discovers his daughter Nadia's inheritance traces through shell companies tied to the arms network — his own family was paid in blood money. POV Bram. Emotional beat: betrayal turning inward, shame and fury.

chapters.title: Renner's Hand
chapters.summary: Renner appears in Belgrade uninvited, offering protection that feels like custody. Bram pretends to accept while copying files. POV Bram. Emotional beat: loyalty curdling into performance.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Petra decodes the recordings' pattern: they were made by a second survivor of the conspiracy, still alive, feeding them breadcrumbs. POV Petra. Emotional beat: hope with a target painted on it.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Voss ambushes Bram and Petra at a border crossing; they escape when a truck driver intervenes, but Petra is wounded and their evidence drive is half-destroyed. POV Bram. Emotional beat: cost made physical.

chapters.title: The Handler
chapters.summary: Voss's handler is revealed mid-rank in the very agency that certified Bram's original crash report. POV Voss. Emotional beat: the machine shown whole for the first time.

chapters.title: Nadia
chapters.summary: Bram surfaces to warn Nadia she may be a liability; their fractured reunion is interrupted by surveillance he can't shake. POV Nadia. Emotional beat: love complicated by inherited guilt.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Following the breadcrumb pattern, Bram meets the living whistleblower: a retired air-traffic controller holding the master ledger. He gives Bram one copy and one warning. POV Bram. Emotional beat: the torch passed.

chapters.title: Renner Unmasked
chapters.summary: Renner reveals himself as the handler's superior — and Bram's old mentor — offering wealth and silence, invoking their shared history. POV Bram. Emotional beat: the theme of loyalty vs. truth at knife-point.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Bram refuses; Renner lets him walk, knowing Voss is already en route. Bram realizes refusal was the trap. POV Bram, closing on Voss boarding a plane. Emotional beat: dread of the inevitable.

chapters.title: Petra's Choice
chapters.summary: Wounded Petra insists on publishing early through a resistant editor while Bram draws Voss away. POV Petra. Emotional beat: courage without guarantee.

chapters.title: The Chase
chapters.summary: A night pursuit through Zurich's rail yards; Bram uses his crash-investigator knowledge of sightlines and braking distances to stay alive. POV Bram. Emotional beat: competence as survival.

chapters.title: Convergence
chapters.summary: Voss corners Bram but hesitates upon learning the ledger implicates Voss's own handlers' paymasters. POV Voss. Emotional beat: the assassin's code cracking.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Bram hijacks a press livestream, uploading the ledger and flight data live as Voss closes in; Renner watches his network burn in real time. POV Bram. Emotional beat: truth as a weapon fired once.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Arrests ripple across three governments; Renner dies by his own hand rather than testify. Voss vanishes, leaving Bram alive — debt unpaid. POV Bram. Emotional beat: victory that tastes like ash.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Bram testifies publicly, naming row twelve and every passenger, refusing anonymity. Nadia sits in the gallery. POV Bram/Nadia. Emotional beat: grief given a public shape.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Months later, Bram sleeps through the night for the first time; he and Nadia donate the tainted inheritance to the victims' families. A final unanswered ring on the burner phone. POV Bram. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept.
